evals.prompt: I installed SigNoz from Anthropic & Partners in Claude Desktop. Its mcp connector says Not added. Configure it for the eu region, and tell me what to do if it was already connected.
evals.expected_output: Agent opens the installed SigNoz plugin's mcp connector, replaces its URL with https://mcp.eu.signoz.cloud/mcp before adding it, and completes OAuth. If it was already added, the agent removes it and re-adds the plugin connector with the new URL. It does not keep a simultaneous second connector or put a remote URL in claude_desktop_config.json.

assertions.text: For a Not added connector, Agent opens the installed SigNoz plugin's mcp connector and sets https://mcp.eu.signoz.cloud/mcp before adding it
assertions.description: The partner plugin connector is configured before its first connection

assertions.text: For an already-added connector, Agent removes it and re-adds the plugin connector with the new URL without keeping a simultaneous second connector
assertions.description: Claude connector changes use the documented remove-and-re-add flow

assertions.text: Agent does not put a remote url entry in claude_desktop_config.json and completes OAuth
assertions.description: Hosted connector configuration stays out of the local stdio file

evals.prompt: I built signoz-mcp-server locally and want Claude Desktop to launch /opt/signoz/signoz-mcp-server over stdio. Configure it with SIGNOZ_URL and an environment-variable placeholder for SIGNOZ_API_KEY.
evals.expected_output: Agent uses claude_desktop_config.json because this is local stdio, creates a signoz mcpServers entry with command=/opt/signoz/signoz-mcp-server, args=[], and env containing SIGNOZ_URL, SIGNOZ_API_KEY placeholder, and LOG_LEVEL. It does not use a remote url field and tells the user to restart Claude Desktop.

assertions.text: The Claude Desktop JSON payload uses command, args, and env for the local stdio server
assertions.description: Local binaries use the stdio registration shape

assertions.text: The Claude Desktop JSON payload does not contain a remote url field
assertions.description: A stdio entry must not be translated into a remote connector payload

assertions.text: Agent avoids writing a real API key and tells the user to restart Claude Desktop
assertions.description: Secrets stay out of tracked config examples and Desktop reloads the local entry

evals.prompt: Check whether my SigNoz MCP setup is working. signoz_search_docs succeeds, but signoz_list_services returns an authentication error.
evals.expected_output: Agent does not use documentation-tool success to judge connectivity. It uses signoz_list_services, classifies the connection as configured but not working, and routes the user to client authentication or credential repair without changing a known-correct endpoint.

assertions.text: Agent does not use signoz_search_docs or signoz_fetch_doc as connectivity probes
assertions.description: Documentation tools do not validate live SigNoz access

assertions.text: Agent uses signoz_list_services as the connectivity probe
assertions.description: The setup check uses the prescribed tenant-backed tool

assertions.text: Agent classifies the state as configured-but-not-working and recommends authentication or credential repair
assertions.description: The endpoint is reachable, but live SigNoz access is not ready

evals.prompt: My Codex SigNoz plugin keeps resetting back to the us endpoint after plugin updates. Fix it for http://localhost:8000/mcp and make it durable.
evals.expected_output: Agent identifies the active Codex package as Agent Plugins v1, updates the bundled mcp.json to http://localhost:8000/mcp while preserving the signoz server key and type=streamable-http, and also creates or updates the native Codex MCP server named signoz using `codex mcp add signoz --url http://localhost:8000/mcp` or the equivalent `[mcp_servers.signoz]` TOML entry. It explains that plugin cache files are versioned and can be regenerated from repository defaults, while the native Codex MCP entry persists across plugin updates. It verifies the effective URL with `codex mcp get signoz` or `codex mcp list`.

assertions.text: Agent identifies versioned plugin cache refresh as the reason the bundled mcp.json reset to the packaged us endpoint
assertions.description: The root cause is cache regeneration from source defaults, not an MCP runtime bug

assertions.text: Agent identifies the active Codex package as Agent Plugins v1 and updates the bundled mcp.json to the resolved endpoint while preserving the signoz server key and type streamable-http
assertions.description: The immediate plugin install is repaired

assertions.text: Agent creates or updates native Codex MCP config for signoz using codex mcp add or [mcp_servers.signoz]
assertions.description: The durable fix lives outside the versioned plugin cache

assertions.text: Agent verifies the effective signoz URL with codex mcp get or codex mcp list
assertions.description: The outcome is checked through Codex's resolved server view

evals.prompt: I installed the portable Agent Plugins v1 package in VS Code. Configure SigNoz at http://signoz.internal:8000/mcp.
evals.expected_output: Agent does not write the non-loopback HTTP URL into the plugin-root mcp.json because Agent Plugins v1 requires HTTPS for non-loopback endpoints. It routes the endpoint to VS Code's native .vscode/mcp.json or user MCP configuration instead, preserving unrelated native servers.

assertions.text: Agent does not write http://signoz.internal:8000/mcp into the portable plugin-root mcp.json
assertions.description: Non-loopback HTTP is invalid in the Agent Plugins v1 remote transport

assertions.text: Agent explains that portable non-loopback endpoints must use HTTPS
assertions.description: The user receives the contract reason rather than a silent failure

assertions.text: Agent configures the endpoint through VS Code native MCP configuration
assertions.description: The unsupported portable value is routed to the identified client's native surface

evals.prompt: My VS Code workspace already has .vscode/mcp.json. Change its SigNoz server to https://mcp.eu.signoz.cloud/mcp without touching plugin files.
evals.expected_output: Agent treats .vscode/mcp.json as the active native VS Code configuration rather than confusing it with the portable plugin-root mcp.json. It updates only the existing signoz server URL, preserves unrelated servers and settings, and gives the VS Code authentication finish step.

assertions.text: Agent reads and updates .vscode/mcp.json instead of skipping it because its basename is mcp.json
assertions.description: The plugin-root exclusion must not hide native VS Code configuration

assertions.text: Agent changes only the existing signoz server URL and preserves unrelated native configuration
assertions.description: The repair avoids duplicate or destructive native entries

assertions.text: Agent provides the VS Code approval or authentication finish step
assertions.description: The native registration is completed through the identified client

evals.prompt: I installed the portable Agent Plugins v1 package. Configure its SigNoz MCP server for the eu2 region.

assertions.text: Agent updates the installed portable plugin-root mcp.json URL to https://mcp.eu2.signoz.cloud/mcp
assertions.description: The portable hosted-region happy path edits the correct registration file

assertions.text: Agent preserves $schema, the signoz server key, and type streamable-http

assertions.text: Agent changes only the URL and provides the identified client's authentication or reload finish step
assertions.description: The update is minimal and completes the client workflow

evals.prompt: I installed the SigNoz marketplace plugin in Claude Code. Its plugin root contains mcp.json as well as .signoz_claude_mcp.json. Configure it for the eu region.
evals.expected_output: Agent uses the explicit Claude Code marketplace installation to identify the Claude Code compatibility package, despite the colocated portable mcp.json. assertions.text: Agent treats the install as the Claude Code compatibility package rather than a portable package
assertions.description: The explicit Claude Code marketplace installation identifies the active package format

assertions.text: Agent updates only mcpServers.mcp.url in the active plugin root's .signoz_claude_mcp.json to https://mcp.eu.signoz.cloud/mcp
assertions.description: The endpoint is written to the active Claude Code plugin registration

assertions.text: Agent preserves the mcp server key and type http and leaves plugin-root mcp.json unchanged
assertions.description: The active Claude registration retains its identity while the inactive portable registration is not mutated

assertions.text: Agent warns that a plugin update can restore the packaged us endpoint, tells the user to rerun setup if that happens, reloads plugins, verifies the effective URL, and authenticates the signoz plugin's mcp server
assertions.description: The finish step covers update reset, reload, and authentication behavior

evals.prompt: I'm running this from the SigNoz plugin in VS Code. I installed it with Chat: Install Plugin From Source from https://github.com/SigNoz/agent-skills. The installed plugin root's plugin.json declares the canonical Agent Plugins schema, and the root also contains mcp.json, .signoz_claude_mcp.json, and .signoz_cursor_mcp.json. A previous run of this setup skill accidentally created a second signoz server in my VS Code user MCP config for http://localhost:8000/mcp. Configure the plugin for that URL and remove the duplicate. There is no .vscode/mcp.json in this workspace.
evals.expected_output: Agent treats the explicit VS Code Install Plugin From Source installation as Agent Plugins v1 even though client-specific compatibility files coexist. It updates only mcpServers.signoz.url in the plugin-root mcp.json to http://localhost:8000/mcp, preserves the portable schema, signoz server key, and type=streamable-http, and leaves the compatibility files unchanged. Because the user explicitly identified the VS Code user signoz entry as an accidental duplicate, it removes only that entry while preserving unrelated user configuration and does not create .vscode/mcp.json. It then tells the user to reload or approve the plugin-provided signoz server without requiring OAuth unless the self-hosted server enables it.

assertions.text: Agent treats the VS Code Install Plugin From Source installation as the portable Agent Plugins v1 package even though client-specific compatibility files are present
assertions.description: Explicit installation provenance identifies the package format

assertions.text: Agent changes only mcpServers.signoz.url in the plugin-root mcp.json to http://localhost:8000/mcp and preserves $schema, the signoz server key, and type streamable-http
assertions.description: The active portable registration is updated without changing its contract

assertions.text: Agent removes only the explicitly confirmed accidental signoz entry from VS Code user MCP configuration, preserves unrelated user settings, does not create .vscode/mcp.json, and leaves .signoz_claude_mcp.json and .signoz_cursor_mcp.json unchanged
assertions.description: The repair removes the known duplicate without modifying unrelated config or inactive compatibility packages

assertions.text: Agent tells the user to reload or approve the plugin-provided signoz server and does not require OAuth for self-hosted MCP unless OAUTH_ENABLED is true
assertions.description: The finish step matches self-hosted VS Code authentication behavior
